title: A Protocol for a Novel Human Ex Vivo Model of Aneurysm
author: Bianco, Di Gregoli, et al.
materials: Timing: 3 h 30 min18.The proximal portion of the artery (approx. 2.5 cm in length) should be cut into five 5 mm rings for subsequent histological processing and wax embedding.19.From the formalin-fixed wax-embedded arterial rings, cut 3 μm sections collected upon adhesive glass microscope slides (two sections per slide).20.To enable assessment of arterial elastin content, perform Elastin van Gieson (EVG) histochemical staining using an automated stainer (such as a Shandon Varistain 24-4 Automatic Slide Stainer) or manual protocol (protocol details are shown in Table 1).Table 1Staining Protocol for EVGSolutionIncubation TimeXylene substitute (such as Clearene)3 × 5 min100% (v/v) alcohol (or industrial methylated spirits)3 × 5 minTap water5 min0.5% (w/v) potassium permanganate10 minDistilled water3 min1% (w/v) oxalic acid5 minDistilled water3 min70% (v/v) alcohol (or industrial methylated spirits)2 min50% (v/v) Millers elastin stain (VWR, Cat#351154S)60 min70% (v/v) alcohol (or industrial methylated spirits)2 minRunning tap water3 minVan Gieson stain (ThermoFisher, LAMB-400-D)30 s100% (v/v) alcohol (or industrial methylated spirits)3 × 5 minXylene substitute (such as Clearene)3 × 5 min21.After EVG staining, coverslip sections using a relevant mounting medium (such as DPX) and visualize the sections using a bright field microscope and acquire images under ×20 magnification.22.Determine the relative amount of elastin (which appears as black under a light microscope) using a computerized image analysis program (such as Image Pro Plus or ImageJ) and express as an average percentage of the arterial cross-sectional area.

steps.title: Prepare Bioreactor Components
steps.instruction: Cut long silicone tubes to the required length, attach a stronger silicone tube, connect all tubes with cannula at both ends, then autoclave; cut short silicone tubes, attach cannula at both ends, then autoclave; autoclave water, forceps, and Sylgard dishes; obtain DMEM and supplement with gentamicin, penicillin, streptomycin, and L‑glutamine; prepare fresh formaldehyde.

substeps.instruction: Cut long silicone tubes to the correct length.
Connect each long tube to a stronger silicone tube (required for the peristaltic pump).
Join all tubes together with a cannula at both ends.
Autoclave the assembled long‑tube assembly.
Cut short silicone tubes to the needed length.
Connect each short tube to a cannula at both ends.
Autoclave the short‑tube assemblies.
Autoclave water, forceps, and Sylgard dishes.
Obtain Dulbecco’s Modified Eagle's Medium (DMEM) and add gentamicin, penicillin, streptomycin, and L‑glutamine.
Prepare a fresh solution of formaldehyde.

steps.title: Assemble Bioreactor
steps.instruction: Sterilize bioreactor chambers in Milton sterilizing solution for at least 2 h, briefly rinse with sterile water, dry under a tissue‑culture hood, then connect a long silicone tube at both ends and attach two short silicone tubes to the inner edges of each chamber.

substeps.instruction: Place bioreactor chambers in Milton sterilizing solution for ≥2 h.
Briefly wash chambers in sterile water.
Transfer chambers to a tissue‑culture hood and allow them to dry.
Connect a long silicone tube to both ends of each chamber.
Connect two short silicone tubes to the inner edges of each chamber.

steps.title: Prepare Artery Segments for EVG
steps.instruction: Excise approximately 2.5 cm of proximal artery, cut into five 5 mm rings, then from formalin‑fixed wax‑embedded rings cut 3 µm sections and place two sections per adhesive glass microscope slide.

substeps.instruction: Cut the proximal arterial segment (~2.5 cm) into five 5 mm rings.
From the formalin‑fixed, wax‑embedded rings, cut 3 µm sections.
Collect two sections on each adhesive glass microscope slide.

steps.title: Elastin van Gieson Staining
steps.instruction: Stain the slides using either an automated Shandon Varistain 24‑4 or the manual protocol: sequential immersions in Clearene (3 × 5 min), 100 % alcohol (3 × 5 min), tap water (5 min), 0.5 % potassium permanganate (10 min), distilled water (3 min), 1 % oxalic acid (5 min), distilled water (3 min), 70 % alcohol (2 min), 50 % Millers elastin stain (VWR Cat#351154S, 60 min), 70 % alcohol (2 min), running tap water (3 min), Van Gieson stain (ThermoFisher LAMB‑400‑D, 30 s), 100 % alcohol (3 × 5 min), and Clearene (3 × 5 min).

substeps.instruction: Clearene (substitute for xylene) – 3 immersions, 5 min each.
100 % alcohol – 3 immersions, 5 min each.
Tap water – 5 min.
0.5 % potassium permanganate – 10 min.
Distilled water – 3 min.
1 % oxalic acid – 5 min.
Distilled water – 3 min.
70 % alcohol – 2 min.
50 % Millers elastin stain (VWR Cat#351154S) – 60 min.
70 % alcohol – 2 min.
Running tap water – 3 min.
Van Gieson stain (ThermoFisher LAMB‑400‑D) – 30 s.
100 % alcohol – 3 immersions, 5 min each.
Clearene – 3 immersions, 5 min each.

steps.title: Mount and Image EVG Slides
steps.instruction: Coverslip the stained sections with DPX mounting medium, view under a bright‑field microscope at 20× magnification, acquire images, and quantify elastin (appears black) using ImageJ or Image Pro Plus, reporting the average percentage of arterial cross‑sectional area.

substeps.instruction: Apply DPX mounting medium and place a coverslip on each slide.
Observe slides with a bright‑field microscope at 20×.
Capture representative images.
Analyze images with ImageJ or Image Pro Plus to calculate the percentage of black elastin area relative to total arterial cross‑section.

steps.title: Prepare Artery Segments for Picrosirius
steps.instruction: From the formalin‑fixed wax‑embedded arterial rings cut 3 µm sections and place two sections per adhesive glass microscope slide (same preparation as for EVG).

substeps.instruction: Cut 3 µm sections from the wax‑embedded arterial rings.
Mount two sections on each adhesive glass slide.

steps.title: Picrosirius Red Staining
steps.instruction: Stain the slides manually: Clearene (3 × 5 min), 100 % alcohol (3 × 5 min), distilled water (3 × 2 min), Picrosirius red solution 0.1 % (w/v) (90 min), 0.01 N HCl (2 × 15 s), distilled water (2 × 2 min), oven‑dry at 37 °C (80 min), 100 % alcohol (1 × 5 min), and Clearene (3 × 5 min). Ensure slides are completely dry before the final 100 % alcohol step.

substeps.instruction: Clearene – 3 immersions, 5 min each.
100 % alcohol – 3 immersions, 5 min each.
Distilled water – 3 immersions, 2 min each.
Picrosirius red solution (0.1 % w/v) – 90 min.
0.01 N hydrochloric acid – 2 immersions, 15 s each.
Distilled water – 2 immersions, 2 min each.
Oven‑dry slides at 37 °C for 80 min.
100 % alcohol – 1 immersion, 5 min (ensure slides are dry before this step).
Clearene – 3 immersions, 5 min each.

steps.title: Mount and Image Picrosirius Slides
steps.instruction: Coverslip the stained sections with DPX, view under a bright‑field polarizing microscope at 20×, acquire images, and quantify collagen (appears red) using ImageJ or Image Pro Plus as the average percentage of arterial cross‑sectional area; additionally, assess fiber thickness/age by measuring the proportion of green versus red fibers, expressing each as a percentage of total collagen.

substeps.instruction: Apply DPX mounting medium and place a coverslip on each slide.
Observe slides with a polarizing bright‑field microscope at 20×.
Capture images under polarized light.
Analyze images to calculate the percentage of red collagen area relative to total arterial cross‑section.
Determine the percentages of green and red fibers to assess collagen fiber thickness/age.
